Jonas — I reviewed the redlines quickly. High level thoughts (we should align on a tight counter so we don't miss their procurement window):

- MSA / liability: we should not accept a blanket 2x fees cap without carveouts. Proposal: keep existing liability cap but add a limited carve for security incidents up to $1M and tie any higher cap to a commercial commitment (e.g., committed minimums).

- DPA: their subprocessors ask is reasonable; agree to a 30-day notification window and a documented objection process for processors handling PHI-level data, but we should keep the default approvals for standard infra providers.

- SOW / SLA: we can commit to a production latency SLA for the managed inference route (hosted/Redwood Dedicated) but not for private on-prem installs. Suggest we offer an SLA only for Dedicated plans and include a separate annex with measurement methodology. For pricing split — recommend a tiered usage schedule rather than a hard train/infer separation.

Next steps: Karthik/Legal to draft a counters packet (MSA + DPA + SOW redlines) and I'll raise with enterprise sales to sign off. Can we aim to have counters out by EOD Monday (Feb 23)?

-Marissa
VP, Partnerships & GTM
Redwood Inference

Team — I pulled together a short redline summary (attached) and a proposed counter language for each doc. Highlights:

- MSA: keep liability cap at $5M or 2x fees whichever is lower; carveouts for willful misconduct and data breaches (up to $2M for data incidents). Proposal text in Redwood_Counters_MSA_v1.docx.
- DPA: 30-day subprocessor notification + ability to object for PHI-level processors. Add requirement for subprocessors to sign our Data Processing Addendum. See Redwood_Counters_DPA_v1.docx.
- SOW Annex A: define latency SLA for Hosted & Dedicated (p90 < 350ms) with service credits for breaches; exclude Private deployment. Clarify pricing appendix to include a training uplift of +25% for model training compute. See Redwood_Counters_SOW_v1.docx.

I also included a short negotiation playbook with fallbacks in redlines_summary.xlsx:
- If NorthDock insists on 2x fees for liability, we push to time-box liability exposure to contract year and link to committed spend.
- If they want full subprocessor approval rights, offer a review period + right to object limited to security/processing of sensitive data only.

I recommend a 30-minute legal sync with NorthDock before finalizing counters. Proposed times: Mon Feb 22 10:00-10:30 PT or Mon Feb 22 15:00-15:30 PT. Which works?

Attachments: redlines_summary.xlsx, Redwood_Counters_MSA_v1.docx, Redwood_Counters_DPA_v1.docx, Redwood_Counters_SOW_v1.docx

Thanks,
